A.claim: No Beal counterexample of signature (2m,2n,3) with m>=4 and n>=4. Even m or even n: signature (4,2n,3) / (2m,4,3), excluded by BCDY 2015 Thm 1. Both odd (>=5): C odd forces a+bi=(u+vi)^3 in Z[i]; on whichever side 3 does not divide the parameter, (s^2)^m+(-eps t)^m=3v^2 with m odd, forbidden by Bennett-Skinner 2004 Thm 1.1 (C=3).

B.claim: Literature state for the residual family (4,4,p), p odd prime: (4,4,3) solved via (n,n,3); (4,4,5) solved via (2n,2n,5) [Bennett 2006]; for general p only the First Case (p does not divide xyz) is proved, for p != 7 (Dieulefait, arXiv:math/0304425, Q-curves and modular congruences). The Second Case is open.
